interest: This file is particularly useful for economic and diplomatic historians because it illustrates how the U.S. State Department monitored both grassroots financial stability and top-level central bank politics in pre-war Japan. The docket entries highlight the vulnerability of regional commercial banks in Nagoya following local bank failures in the early 1930s, as well as Ministry of Finance regulatory measures to prevent capital flight through foreign currency deposit prohibitions. Furthermore, the records concerning the New York agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank and the political fallout surrounding the appointment and resignation of Bank of Japan Governor Seihin Ikeda illuminate the mounting tensions between Japanese financial leaders and the nation's aggressive military policy in China.
overview: This file comprises the Department of State's central decimal file 894.516 ("Banks. Banking in Japan") from 1930 to 1937, preserved as two "List of Papers" docket sheets that record incoming and outgoing correspondence, consular reports, interdepartmental memoranda, and cross-reference entries. The documents indexed span sub-numbers 37 through 45 and cover key aspects of Japanese banking and financial policy during the early Showa period, including consular surveys of regional commercial banking in Nagoya and Aichi Prefecture, the local fallout of minor bank failures, and Ministry of Finance regulations prohibiting unauthorized foreign currency deposits. The file also tracks diplomatic correspondence regarding inquiries into the employment of Chinese nationals in Japanese banks, Treasury Department conferences concerning the New York agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank, and internal State Department commentary on major leadership transitions at the Bank of Japan, notably the appointment and subsequent resignation of Governor Seihin Ikeda amidst controversy surrounding Japan's military policy in China.

subfiles.about: Docket sheet indexing reports and cross-references on regional Japanese banking facilities, bank failures in Aichi, and foreign currency deposit regulations from 1930 to 1932.
subfiles.summary: This List of Papers sheet (Form DS-46) indexes documents sub-numbered 37 through 41 filed under decimal file 894.516 between March 1930 and September 1932. It records consular reports from Nagoya by Preston on commercial banking institutions (including Nagoya Bank, Meiji/Mojji Bank, and Aichi Bank), and by Chapman on the failure of two local banks and public statements by the Governor of Aichi Prefecture to restore depositor confidence. Additionally, it lists cross-reference notes to files on Yokohama Specie Bank losses following a change of government, general reports on Japanese banking conditions, and legal decrees prohibiting unauthorized foreign currency deposits.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Banks. Banking in Japan (Sub. Nos. 37–41)

subfiles.about: Continuation docket sheet recording correspondence, memoranda, and cross-references regarding Chinese bank employees and Bank of Japan leadership from 1934 to 1937.
subfiles.summary: This continuation sheet (Sheet #5) records documents sub-numbered 42 through 45 in decimal file 894.516 from September 1934 to July 1937. It indexes diplomatic correspondence involving Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and State Department officials in response to inquiries by Mrs. Wortham James regarding the employment of Chinese nationals in Japanese banks, as well as a Treasury Department conference memorandum on the New York agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank. Furthermore, it records cross-reference entries concerning the appointment of Seihin Ikeda as Governor of the Bank of Japan succeeding Eigo Fukai in February 1937, and Ikeda's resignation in July 1937 amidst speculation linking his departure to disagreements over Japan's military policy in China.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Banks - Banking - Japan, Sheet #5 (Sub. Nos. 42–45)
